svg.title: A migration happens one URL at a time
svg.desc: Diagram of how Google Search processes a site migration, one URL at a time, with documented failure points at each of five steps. Step 1, Old URL recrawled (Every old URL, at least once): fails when server errors (5xx, 429) make Google’s crawlers slow down; rarely crawled URLs move last: weeks to never for a refresh. Step 2, Redirect followed (301 or 308, straight to the target): fails when target returns a 404, or many URLs land on the home page (soft 404); chains beyond 3 to 5 hops; a 302 or 307 is only a weak signal; a JavaScript redirect is missed if rendering fails. Step 3, New URL crawled (More heavily than usual, for a while): fails when development noindex or robots.txt blocks are still live; the new server cannot absorb the extra crawling. Step 4, Canonical chosen (New URL picked over the old one): fails when canonicals, internal links, sitemaps or hreflang still name old URLs. Step 5, Signals consolidated (Old URL fades from results): fails when templates, content or platform changed on the same day; redirects removed early: Change of Address runs 180 days; Google says keep them at least a year. Google: a move is complete only when Googlebot has visited every old and new URL at least once. Permanent redirects lose no PageRank.

Each old URL goes through five steps in Google Search. Documented failure points at each step.
STEP IN GOOGLE SEARCH

Every old URL, at least once

A JavaScript redirect is missed if rendering fails

Old URL fades from results
Templates, content or platform changed on the same day
Redirects removed early: Change of Address runs 180 days; Google says keep
them at least a year
Google: a move is complete only when Googlebot has visited every old and new URL at least once. Permanent redirects lose no PageRank.
